solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Directed opening of Cor Blimey! — new English play

indicators.note: a director arranges actors on stage

explanation.surface: A startled director shouts a Cockney oath at the start of rehearsals for a new English play.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor blimey is a Cockney exclamation of surprise; here it is split, with only its first word shortened to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of Shakespeare's late romances, so play stands for it.

clue.text: Clubs briefly entertain writer and philosopher

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: AMUSE with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: Nightclubs host a writer and philosopher for a short turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs reads as nightclubs; in crosswords it is usually the card suit, abbreviated C.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the author of The Outsider was both novelist and existentialist thinker.

clue.text: High speed on wide street upset sick Italian diplomat

indicators.note: to upset is to tip over, and in a down clue a word tipped over reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Mach 1, the speed of sound, with the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An Italian diplomat, sick after racing along a boulevard, is thrown about.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing a digit as the look-alike letter (1 as I, 0 as O) is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Florentine author of The Prince served his city as an envoy.

clue.text: Time and arithmetic problems boosted scholar

indicators.note: boosted means pushed up, and in a down clue a word pushed up reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time spent on sums has given a student's grades a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Boosted only works as a reversal because this is a down clue, where up means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dutch humanist of the Renaissance is the archetypal learned man.

clue.text: Some paint and emulsion at the same time

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying inside the words

blocks.note: starts after the first two letters of paint and stops three letters into emulsion

explanation.surface: A decorator applies some paint and emulsion together.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words: paINT AND EMulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: two things done in tandem go together, side by side at once.

clue.text: Suppose former partner nibbled on the ear?

indicators.note: what lands on the ear is what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex nibbling someone's ear, which you might suppose is a sign of lingering affection.
explanation.walkthrough: On the ear pretends to say where the nibbling happened; it actually tells you to listen to the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: I expect so means I suppose so.

clue.text: Unearth detective uniform hidden by family doctor

indicators.note: something hidden by a thing is tucked inside it, so the letter goes inside the next word

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner, the British family doctor
U is uniform in the phonetic alphabet; it goes inside GP

explanation.surface: A detective uncovers a uniform that the family doctor had concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP (general practitioner) is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both literal (from the soil) and figurative (discovering facts).

clue.text: Letter opener?

blocks.note: the surface wants a thing made of paper; the setter means correspondence in general
not a knife that slits envelopes but the words a formal letter begins with

explanation.surface: A knife for slitting envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener is a paper knife; the question mark says to read it as the words that open a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional salutation is literally the first thing in a formal letter.

clue.text: Regularly good at beach cricket here?

indicators.note: letters taken regularly come at even intervals, here every other one

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a place for a game of cricket on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only an example, hence the question mark: Goa is an Indian state known for its beaches, in a cricket-mad country.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Indian coastal state is famous for beaches, and India plays cricket everywhere.

clue.text: After climbing mountain, Bond gets an assignment

indicators.note: climbing means going up, and in a down clue a word going up reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: James Bond climbs a mountain and is given his next mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like 007, and the mountain climb fits a spy film; in fact bond is the verb, to stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a work placement is a job you are assigned to, often temporary.

clue.text: Second brew — fine coffee

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'just a mo'
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A second pot of tea, then a good coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'half a mo' and 'a cup of cha' are everyday slang for a moment and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the high-quality bean first shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Big boss mostly crazy to have backed corporation first

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
backed means sent backwards, so the word is read from its end
first puts the reversed word at the front, before the other piece

blocks.note: a corporation is jocular British slang for a pot belly
BANANAS, crazy, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A crazy boss wants the company to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation reads as the company; it is old slang for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the top banana is the most important person in an organisation.

clue.text: Some cut off from this outfit for pool competition

indicators.note: letters that are off are out of kilter, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: swimming is the sport of a pool gala

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a piece off a swimsuit to wear at a gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as a sum: take SOME CUT, jumbled, away from the answer and SWIMMING is left, the pool competition.
explanation.definitionFit: This refers to the answer itself, and the outfit is what you wear in the pool.

clue.text: Open University behind IT’s development

indicators.note: something in development is changing shape, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: The Open University is behind a new IT project.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning institution, so Open looks tied to University; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a person: frank and unreserved.

clue.text: Showered in loo building around one

explanation.surface: Someone took a shower in an outside toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is two words run together, so the enclosed letter ends up at the seam between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Showered in the sense of heaped generously upon someone, as with praise or gifts.

clue.text: Become disillusioned, I shed a few pounds outside hospital

blocks.note: to lose fat; it wraps around the I
H = hospital, as on road signs; it goes at the end

explanation.surface: A dieter becomes disillusioned after only losing a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is a letter of the wordplay, not the speaker: it slips inside the dieting phrase, and the hospital sign follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to stop believing in someone or something is to become disillusioned with it.

clue.text: Let me see setter’s fur

blocks.note: er is the pause of someone thinking

explanation.surface: Someone asks to look at the crossword setter's fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Let me see is not about looking: it is the hesitation you say while thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the stoat's white winter coat, used to trim royal and judicial robes.

clue.text: Aloofness of France’s top couturier turning over his cash

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
something turned over is flipped end to end, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: A leading French fashion designer is snooty as he counts his takings.
explanation.walkthrough: France's top reads as a leading French figure, but it is simply the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French for coldness of manner, used in English much as aloofness is.

clue.text: Seductive dancer Oscar married in Cheshire town

blocks.note: Sale is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England
O is Oscar in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer called Oscar marries in a north of England town.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar also hints at Oscar Wilde, who wrote a play about this dancer, but here it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the biblical figure whose dance of the seven veils won her John the Baptist's head.

clue.text: British upper-class spy circles criminal order

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it

blocks.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation
U = upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A posh British spy keeps watch on a gang of criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: Circles is the verb: the spy surrounds the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Order here is a system of government, and rule by a lawless crowd is a criminal one.

clue.text: Doctor corrupt photos that might be produced in court

definitions.text: that might be produced in court

indicators.note: something corrupt has been tampered with, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Doctored photos are shown as evidence in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Court means a tennis or squash court, not a law court, and Doctor is a noun, not the verb to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a soft stroke dropping just over the net is played on a tennis court.

clue.text: Artist/playwright penning article

explanation.surface: A figure who both paints and writes plays is at work on an article.
explanation.walkthrough: Penning suits a playwright writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who paints pictures is an artist.

clue.text: Endless farce exposed banal secrets

indicators.note: without ends: the word loses its first and last letters
something exposed has had its covering stripped off, so the word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: farce without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A farce drags on, revealing only trivial gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Exposed reads as revealed, but it means peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: arcana are mysteries known only to initiates.

clue.text: One lying across large mountainous region surrounding city of rock, the silly goose!

indicators.note: the liar lies across the letter, stretched over it on both sides

blocks.note: L = large; it goes inside FIBBER
Gib = Gibraltar, the Rock; it goes inside TIBET

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a daft traveller who has been fibbing about a mountain trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, and Gib is its short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a flighty, frivolous, chattering person is a silly goose.

clue.text: Lines packed into day’s material

indicators.note: something packed into a case is put inside it

blocks.note: L = line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone has a day packed with lines to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of day's links the wordplay to the definition, as in day has.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the fine silk net used for veils and tutus is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: I clean out wound to protect against infection

indicators.note: wound is the past of wind, so the letters have been twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse cleans out a wound so it will not get infected.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound reads as an injury, which fits the nurse; it is the verb wind, as in wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving a vaccine primes the body against a disease.

clue.text: Blade cut off pig’s head

indicators.note: cut off means removed, so a letter is chopped away
the head of a word is its first letter, the one that goes

blocks.note: a boar is a male pig; its first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A knife is used to cut off a pig's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Blade is not a knife; it is the flat end of an oar, standing for the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A part for the whole: rowers call the oar by its flat end, the blade.

clue.text: Write off the entire amount

blocks.note: a verb: to wreck a car beyond repair

explanation.surface: Someone cancels a whole debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Write off suggests cancelling a debt; the other sense is the insurer's write-off, a car smashed beyond repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for wrecking a vehicle completely, and the ordinary noun for a whole sum.

clue.text: Host’s delivery of treasure trove

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is how the words come out when spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a hoard is a treasure trove

explanation.surface: A host hands over a stash of treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Host means a great crowd, not someone giving a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a heavenly host or a host of people is a great multitude.

clue.text: Broadcast game’s link between two places

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A televised game connects two towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular flight service between two places works as a bridge through the air.
